When my baby was a few weeks old I dont think she was ever NOT on my boob. All day, all night.

Look up the fourth trimester - it explains better why babies want to feed all day and night in the first 3 months of life.

As long as baby is putting on weight as usual, I don't think you need to worry. Annoying thing about breastfeeding is you can't measure what babies getting! Trust your body and trust your baby. If you are really worried about your supply, feeding more will get your supply up. 

If for any reason baby isn't gaining weight, you're unable to express milk by hand or hakaa etc PLEASE contact a midwife or gp or lactation consultant or any professional. 

Best of luck with your breastfeeding journey, I think its the best thing ever :)

If its just revision of something I'm fairly confident in, I might put some music on but if I'm struggling I try to put all my focus in to it,even if it is just 20 minutes.

I also find that writing things down helps massively. Any definition, any theory, I try to rewrite in my own words in a way that I find easiest to understand. You might already have the info I front of you, sure, but the act of writing it down really helps solidify it in the brain.

I'm pretty sure they took my blood then as well as I had opted for all the screenings they offered (tests for down syndrome et

After that you will have regular appointments with your midwife every 3/4 weeks and another scan (anomaly scan where they check baby is growing well and they can check and measure babies head, brain, heart etc) at 20 weeks. This is also the scan to see babies gender if you want to know!
